messages:
morgan: Quick heads-up — after the kernel selection bump (v2.3.1) we're seeing a 15-20% p99 increase on short-sequence chat workloads. profiler attached, but high-level: more frequent small allocs and higher freelist churn. :eyes:

sasha: Can you paste the profiler output? is it alloc count or fragmentation (wasted bytes)?

morgan: paste below — it's basically the timeline from gpu-prof with allocator events. noticing lots of small arena splits around logits/scratchpad size.

```
GPU_TRACE summary:
- total requests: 120k
- median latency: 42ms
- p99 latency: 210ms (prev: 175ms)
- allocator ops: alloc=28k free=27.6k (spikes per batch)
- avg freelist blocks per stream: 48 -> 103 after bump
- scratchpad avg occupancy: 68% -> 45% (more small allocs)
- KV cache hit rate unchanged
```

liam: hmm looks like the kernel changed workspace sizing requirement. new kernels ask for slightly larger temp buffers, so allocator splits differently and increases fragmentation.

ana: (typo — ana): we also changed batching heuristic to try more aggressive batch growth for latency-targeted routes — could interact with allocator by increasing live set variation.

ana: quick question: are logits buffers being reused across sequences in the same stream or freed each request?

morgan: currently we do per-request free of logits and activations to keep memory pressure low for mixed workloads. we had a reuse path but turned it off in the kernel bump because of a correctness scare.

ryan: suggestion: re-enable sticky-logits reuse with a max-age eviction and per-stream freelist limits. that reduces churn for short sequences. also track fragmentation by size-class.

sasha: agree. also try compaction for freelist: when free bytes > X% of arena, coalesce or return to OS (or cudaFree) for scratchpads. cheap win.

morgan: running two experiments this morning: 1) sticky logits reuse (reuse up to 3 batches per stream) + per-class cap, 2) arena compaction threshold at 60% free bytes -> cudaFree on large slabs.

devbot: scheduled experiment jobs: infra/experiments/alloc-freelist-2026-04-12
- exp-id: alloc-freelist-0426
- configs: sticky_logits=true; freelist_compaction=0.6; max_workspace_bytes=24MB

liam: small note: for compaction path make sure we respect kernel alignment. new kernels request 3 alignments: 256, 512, 4096 for different ops. coalescing must maintain alignment.

ana: also log per-request freelist hits in metrics (counter) so we can correlate p99 with reuse ratio.

morgan: ran experiment 1 locally: p99 improved to ~180ms (partial), alloc ops down 40%. memory transient increased a bit but within Dedicated headroom.

ryan: good. for OOM mitigation, consider spill-to-host for large scratchpad allocations (only for non-critical fast paths) — will keep p99 stable when a bad request spikes transient memory.

devbot: note: added metric 'alloc.freelist_hit_ratio' and 'alloc.compaction_runs' to prometheus job.

morgan: next steps: (a) roll sticky logits reuse to canary with max-age 3 and per-stream cap 2MB, (b) enable freelist compaction on non-hosted clusters to measure longer runs, (c) add regression test that simulates kernel workspace variance and asserts freelist fragmentation < 30%.

sasha: one more: add a lightweight heap walker that samples arenas every minute and emits top-3 size-classes by fragmentation. will help decide quantized class boundaries.

ana: I'll own the metrics dashboards for this. will add a per-route view (short seq vs long seq) so we can see the batching heuristic interaction.

morgan: perfect. if the canary is stable for ~24h we'll roll cluster-wide. thanks all. :thumbsup:
